leading_positions.synthesis: Both prefer Balasubramanian and Klenerman for massively parallel sequencing by synthesis (reversible terminators, clustered single molecules), and both treat it as mature. They differ on the rest of the configuration: Aqvist lists it alone, with B005 and B012 as alternatives, while Linke pairs it with a nanopore part (B001) and lists B034 and B012 as alternatives. Both exclude Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing from the core credit, but Aqvist notes that Rothberg or the Mayer and Ju contributions might need to be revisited. Chabes and Sparr list B011 only as an alternative, and Chabes questions how much of it is chemistry rather than platform engineering.

Both prefer targeted protein degradation as a designable chemical reaction that recruits E3 ligases, and both name Crews and Deshaies. They differ on Handa and the molecular-glue (cereblon) arm: Chabes includes Handa and treats the glue arm as the strongest evidence of maturity, while Aili excludes Handa and says he would not defend that boundary strongly. Aili pairs B034 with base editing (B012, Liu); Chabes lists B034 alone. Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Sparr list B034 as an alternative; no member other than Chabes and Aili prefers it in the configuration.

Both prefer Liu alone as the second part, citing the cytosine and adenine base editors, and both worry about the 2020 CRISPR prize. They pair it with different first parts (B034 for Aili, B053 Buchwald-Hartwig amination for Somfai). Aili sees base editing as a designable chemical conversion; Somfai doubts how much is new chemistry, since a natural deaminase is repurposed through protein engineering. Both defend Liu alone against Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID), on the grounds that the adenine editor has no counterpart there.

Only the chair prefers nanopore sensing, as a second part credited to Bayley alone. Others who commented (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr) accept the physical principle and maturity but object to attribution among Kasianowicz, Branton (deceased), Deamer, Akeson and Bayley, and to naming one person. Linke's file does not state Bayley's status; other members raised it and it is not established in the files.

Brzezinski prefers Gray and Winkler for long-range protein electron transfer, as a quantitative physical mechanism confirmed for decades. He concedes that no colleague ranked it in the opening round. Aili and Zou accept the science but ask about breadth and new capability; Sparr finds the two-name attribution persuasive but ranks condensates above it.

Somfai prefers Buchwald and Hartwig for palladium-catalysed C-N coupling, citing 25 years of confirmation and industrial use. The open points are Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling and the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Aqvist argues that C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution from the C-C couplings of 2010. Only two members ranked it in the opening round.

Sparr prefers Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen for biomolecular phase separation, as a new organising principle for cells. Linke questions the in vivo evidence, and Sparr herself concedes that it is uneven. Pappu and Mittag are left out by the three-name cap.

Zou prefers Corma, Davis and Zones for molecular-sieve catalyst design, as structure determining function with large industrial deployment. Somfai's file does not address it. Zou flags the 2025 MOF prize as a timing problem, notes that Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are excluded, and discloses proximity of her own field.

areas_of_agreement: No ballot has more than two explicit supporters in the round-1 configurations: B011 (Aqvist, Linke), B034 (Aili, Chabes) and B012 (Aili, Somfai) each have two, and B001, B028, B053, B026 and B051 each have one. Nothing near the five-vote majority is visible.

Several members respond to B011 as mature, with a clean attribution: Aqvist, Linke, Brzezinski, Zou and Sparr describe the Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair as the cleanest attribution or chemical invention among the high-impact candidates, though only two prefer it.
Members broadly accept that the mechanism behind B034 is well defined and independently reproduced; the disagreement is about maturity and credit, not about whether the science is real.

Members describe the mature candidates (B011, B053, B028, B051) as better established than the newer ones (B034, B012, B026), and several treat the lack of an approved PROTAC drug, the short clinical record of base editing and the unresolved in vivo status of condensates as the main maturity questions.
Several members wish to verify priority claims (Kosugi, Kondo and Nishida, Rothberg, Hajdu and Neutze) against the expert reports before relying on recollection.
scientific_disputes: Whether B034 is one achievement or two: the bifunctional PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon and molecular-glue mechanism (Handa) are treated differently by Chabes (include both) and Aili (PROTAC concept, Handa optional); Brzezinski asks that this be settled first.

Whether base editing (B012) is a new chemical principle or an application of the 2020 CRISPR discovery plus protein engineering of an existing deaminase (Aili for the former, Somfai, Linke and Chabes uneasy about the latter).

Whether sequencing by synthesis (B011) is a chemical invention or a platform and medicine achievement; Aqvist, Chabes, Zou and Sparr each raise this in some form, and Linke raises it against his own configuration.
Whether condensates (B026) are demonstrably phase-separated and functional in vivo, or in part overexpression artefacts (Sparr concedes the point; Linke presses it).

Whether breadth of consequence (a new tool or modality) or depth of mechanism (a quantitative physical rule) should weigh more, as in B028 and B034 versus B051, B012 and B011; Aili and Zou frame it this way against B028.
attribution_disputes: B034: Crews, Deshaies and Handa (Chabes) versus Crews and Deshaies (Aili); Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito are excluded under any three-person cap.

B011: the Cambridge pair (Balasubramanian, Klenerman; Aqvist and Linke) versus adding Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing) or Mayer and Ju (clustering and terminator chemistry). Aqvist says priority among Solexa, Lynx and 454 rests on his own recollection.
B012: Liu alone (Aili, Somfai) versus including Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID); Komor and Gaudelli did the founding experiments but are not proposed.

B001: Kasianowicz, Branton (deceased), Deamer, Akeson and Bayley; Linke proposes Bayley alone, and Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Somfai and Sparr find that hard to defend. Other members say Bayley's status needs checking.
B026: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag for sequence grammar.
B053: Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling (and possibly Migita) as priority against Buchwald and Hartwig.
B051: Corma, Davis and Zones versus Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis.
B042 (an alternative for Brzezinski and Zou): the concept (Hajdu, Neutze) versus the experimental realisation (Chapman, Fromme, Schlichting); Brzezinski and Zou propose different third names.

Similar-looking proposals differ in what they credit: B011 and B001 both concern reading DNA, but in different laureates and citations (reversible-terminator chemistry versus pore engineering); B034 trios differ by Handa.
maturity_disputes: B034: no approved PROTAC drug, but cereblon-based glue drugs have a long patient record (Chabes, Linke); Aili, Brzezinski, Sparr and Zou treat the clinical verdict as early.
B012: six years after the 2020 CRISPR prize, with a short clinical safety record (Aili, Somfai and Linke raise it; Chabes asks how much weight the 2020 prize should carry).
B026: unresolved in vivo evidence for condensates (Sparr, Linke).
B011, B028, B053 and B051: described as mature, with decades of confirmation, but B053 and B051 carry optics concerns from the 2010 cross-coupling and 2025 MOF prizes (Somfai, Zou).
B005 (an alternative for Aqvist and Zou): perovskite stability and disputed priority among six names (Aqvist, Zou).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Zou Xiaodong: her research on electron crystallography of zeolites and porous materials is close to B051, which she prefers; she offers recusal on B051 for the committee to decide.
Zou Xiaodong and Peter Brzezinski are Stockholm University colleagues; Brzezinski notes it but sees no conflict.

Peter Brzezinski: his research on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is close to B028 and to the proton-coupled electron transfer candidate; he flags field proximity, not a personal tie.
Heiner Linke (chair): interest in molecular motors and ratchets is close to enzyme-ratcheted nanopore sequencing (B001); he flags possible bias, not a recusal issue.
Emma Sparr: her research on lipid and protein self-assembly is adjacent to condensate work (B026); she notes shared Lund affiliation with Linke and Somfai.
Johan Aqvist, Daniel Aili, Andrei Chabes and Peter Somfai: each reports no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: Should B034 be a single citation, and if so, does it cover Crews and Deshaies only (PROTAC concept) or also Handa (cereblon and molecular glues)? Chabes and Aili should each say what their citation excludes.

Is sequencing by synthesis (B011) a chemistry discovery as distinct from a platform or medicine achievement, and can a citation be worded that rewards the reversible-terminator chemistry rather than the field? Should Rothberg, Mayer or Ju appear at all?

For B001, can the committee identify a defensible and living set of laureates from Kasianowicz, Deamer, Akeson, Bayley and Branton (deceased), and what exactly would each be credited for? If not, should Linke withdraw it from his configuration?
Is base editing (B012) distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize in principle, not only in application, and does Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID alter the credit to Liu alone?
Is a two-part prize preferred to a single-field prize, and which pairings (B011 with B001, B034 with B012, B053 with B012) can reach five members?

For the candidates that only one member prefers (B028, B053, B026, B051), what would the other seven members need to see to rank them above B011, B034 or B012? Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr and Zou are asked to name a second-choice configuration that could draw wider support.
Should Zou recuse from B051, and does the 2025 MOF prize rule out a porous-materials prize this year?
Which priority claims (Kosugi, Rothberg, Kondo and Nishida, Hajdu and Neutze) can the expert reports settle, so that members need not rely on recollection?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 configurations are widely dispersed: eight different first parts, no ballot preferred by more than two members, and no configuration close to five. B011, B034 and B012 each have two explicit supporters, B011 and B034 are the most-cited alternatives, and the main recurring obstacles are attribution (B034, B001, B012), the 2020 CRISPR prize (B012) and clinical or in vivo maturity (B034, B026). Round 2 should therefore focus on narrowing the set and fixing a defensible citation for each surviving configuration. This summary counts only positions that are explicit in the eight files.
